pool.text: The city was founded during the Land Run and grew within hours.
Oklahoma City University was founded by the United Methodist Church.
Oklahoma City surpassed Guthrie as the new state population center and hub.
The discovery of oil within the city limits transformed the area.
The Tower Theater was built on 23rd Street near Route 66.
WKY-TV went on the air as a television station.
The city government launched a Great Annexation Drive expanding area.
Patience Latting was elected mayor, becoming the first female mayor.
Six employees were murdered at a Sirloin Stockade restaurant.
The bankruptcy of Penn Square Bank caused severe economic hardship.
The city passed the Metropolitan Area Projects redevelopment package.
Timothy McVeigh detonated a bomb in front of the federal building.
A violent F5 tornado impacted parts of Oklahoma City and communities.
The museum opened across the street from the governor's mansion.
The university opened the Wanda L Bass School of Music.
The restoration of the historic Skirvin Hotel was completed.
The Oklahoma City Thunder relocated from Seattle to Oklahoma City.
Voters approved the MAPS 3 proposal including Core to Shore elements.
Oklahoma City achieved a rank of 45 in a community health study.
Oklahoma City took last place in an annual community health ranking.
